structure:
repos/trade-imports-performance-tests is the k6 performance-test suite for INS (dockerStack: null; it runs against the stack, not in it). Layout: src/suites/ (12 *.k6.js entry suites: smoke, peak-day, background-volume, design-target and others), src/k6/ (23 modules, about 4,800 lines: the journey walkers, INS front-door sessions, readiness, eventing, resilience, stub ceilings, reporting), src/config/ (catalogues: journey-endpoints.js names every step's endpoint tags, endpoints.js the endpoint catalogue, smoke.js the journey set bases such as setBase '/live-animals', target.js the target URLs, plus thresholds, traffic and call-ratio config), src/lib/ (helpers: redirects.js parses set roots and create paths, forms.js and form-fill.js fill journey forms, address-book.js), reports/ (generated run output), compose/, scripts/ and a 1,049-line README. Pages are reached by following links and forms from the set root, so routes appear as set bases, create paths, endpoint tags and walker.open calls rather than a route table. The scope is the animals frontend and INS front-door routes the k6 scripts request: the live-animals set root (opened as the animals journey dashboard, which inc-129 stops rendering when the notification list moves to the INS front door), the create path and notification journey pages, and the INS dashboard and address book. Cut in 2 parts along that seam: the animals live-animals journey (about 1,500 lines) and the INS front door (about 1,300 lines). Left out: the high-risk plants journey (src/k6/high-risk-plants.js and the plants steps; journeys.js is shared, and only its live-animals and shared-page behaviour is claimed), load shapes, thresholds, SLAs, stub ceilings, resilience faults, eventing and dead-letter checks, reference-data reads, design-target and generator reporting, src/suites/ wiring, reports/, compose/, scripts/, CI workflows and the *.test.js unit tests (read only to confirm a route, never claimed on their own).

Extracted in 2 parts:
Part 1, Live-animals journey routes: Part 1, Live-animals journey routes. Read in full: src/k6/journeys.js (552 lines, the shared notification walker: dashboard, create, draft sessions, review and declaration, read-back, amend, cancel-amend, backend replay), src/k6/live-animals.js (232 lines, the 13 live-animals draft steps, the re-edit list and the amend edit), src/k6/journey-pages.js (167 lines, page path, save check, choice and address-picker helpers), src/k6/documents.js (146 lines, the accompanying-documents upload, status poll and continue), src/k6/pages.js (172 lines, the walker that opens, posts, submits, uploads and reaches pages), src/config/journey-endpoints.js (103 lines, the endpoint tags per step and the shared-page tags), src/config/smoke.js (112 lines, JOURNEYS set bases, identity and scenarios), src/config/test-data.js (73 lines, commodity search, document date and scan timing), src/lib/redirects.js (120 lines, create-path id parsing, staleAction and sign-in hop rules), src/lib/forms.js (52 lines), src/lib/form-fill.js (111 lines, blank-field answer rules and the d/m/yyyy date writer), src/lib/redirects.test.js (154 lines, read only to confirm routes and the draft id shape) and the workspace page docs/repos/trade-imports-performance-tests.md (134 lines, context). There is no route table: routes appear as the set base '/live-animals', the create path '<setBase>/notifications', the notification base '<setBase>/notifications/<id>' and the page slugs each step opens under it. Covered: the journey dashboard at the set root and its search by ?referenceNumber=, the create POST and the id read from its redirect, the hub at the notification base, all 13 live-animals steps in STEP_ENDPOINTS order (origin, commodities with search, consignment-details, commodities/identification, import-reason, additional-details, accompanying-documents with upload and status, addresses with five party pickers and their search, cph-number, port-of-entry, transit-countries with add, transporters, consignment/contact/select) with every field name and value posted, the re-edit list, notification-view, declaration and its save, confirmation, amend, cancel-amend and its save, the three backend requests (fulfilments, list by referenceNumber, replace), the staleAction and sign-in redirect rules, and every check name the scripts make. The scripts assert no page heading, caption or copy: their only text check is that the dashboard search page contains the reference number. Left to part 2: the INS front door (sign-in pages, INS dashboard, address book). Left out by the partition: the high-risk plants journey and harness internals (think time, traffic classes, metrics, redirect-hop limits, eventing). The suite has no germinal-products journey anywhere under src/.
Part 2, INS front-door routes: Part 2, INS front-door routes. Read in full: src/k6/front-door.js (286 lines: openInsDashboard, the dashboard-only session, the address-book session's nine page requests plus the optional worst-case search, and ensurePerfAddress), src/k6/browser-session.js (304 lines: the browser-like session that follows redirects, signs in at the Defra ID stub's sign-in page and reads each page's h1, crumb, hidden fields and form inputs), src/k6/returning-session.js (123 lines: the returning visit that keeps one browser and re-authenticates through Defra ID back to the page it asked for), src/k6/readiness.js (111 lines: the readiness probes, two of them against the INS frontend), src/k6/background-volume.js (177 lines: the INS read-model and journey-backend count reads, the address-book count read off the INS address-book page's results label, and the background add-address form), src/lib/address-book.js (32 lines: reading an address id from list links, and the worst-case search term), src/config/endpoints.js (173 lines: the endpoint catalogue; INS and live-animals frontend page names are claimed here once as a catalogue, plants and stub names are out of scope), src/config/target.js (233 lines: target URLs, local ports, the CDP gateway and the prod refusal), and the two unit tests browser-session.test.js and address-book.test.js (read only to confirm routes such as /auth/sign-in and /auth/callback). For the posted values I also looked up PERF_ADDRESS, ADDRESS_BOOK_LOAD_NAME_PREFIX and READINESS in src/config/smoke.js, WORST_CASE_SEARCH_LENGTH in src/config/test-data.js, and the returning-session entries in src/config/design-target.js. Covered: the INS dashboard at '/' and its sign-in hop and check; the dashboard-only and returning sessions; the address-book list, worst-case search, add, search, view, edit and delete requests with fields, values and checks; the two INS readiness probes and the four other readiness probes as context; the background-volume reads; the endpoint catalogue's INS and animals page names; and the target URL rules. Live-animals journey step behaviour is part 1's.
